solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Iron and gold clothing of chair's occupant

indicators.note: clothing something means wrapping round it, so one word is dressed around another

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them
taken as written, sitting inside the ironing word
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Something about metals dressing whoever sits in a chair, perhaps a throne-like seat.
explanation.walkthrough: PR(OF)ESS + OR. 'Chair' is the academic post, not furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A professor holds a university chair, the named senior post in a department.

clue.text: Frank, like Luke and John

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a frank is the stamped mark on a letter
second meaning: these Gospels come after Mark's in the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone named Frank is compared to two apostles.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two parts, 'post' meaning after and Mark the Gospel; Luke and John follow Mark in the New Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Franking a letter stamps an official mark showing postage paid, which is what a postmark is.

clue.text: Noises coming from pens using old writing materials

parts.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
inks are what you write with

explanation.surface: Scratchy sounds from fountain pens loaded with antique ink.
explanation.walkthrough: The pens are pigpens, not writing implements, which the surface tries hard to suggest.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigs kept in pens grunt, and those grunting sounds are oinks.

clue.text: An overdue converted try

indicators.note: something converted has been changed into a different form, so these letters are remade

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A rugby try finally converted after a long wait.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby a try is 'converted' by kicking a goal after it, so the surface is all sport.
explanation.definitionFit: An endeavour is an attempt, the same sense as a try.

clue.text: Insignificant wound is no handicap

definitions.meaning: second meaning: in golf a ... player has a handicap of zero

explanation.surface: A minor injury that won't hold anyone back.
explanation.walkthrough: In golf, playing off scratch means having no handicap at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A scratch is a slight surface wound, and scratch is the golfing term for a zero handicap.

clue.text: Shipyard worker from Tyne heartlessly thrown in Clyde, say

indicators.note: without a heart means the middle of the word is cut out
in places the jumbled pair inside the example word that follows

parts.note: the Clyde is a Scottish river, flowing through Glasgow

indicators.note: thrown means tossed about, so the remaining letters land in a new order

parts.note: the river name with its middle pair removed

explanation.surface: A shipbuilder from Tyneside dumped in a Glasgow river, both famous shipbuilding rivers.
explanation.walkthrough: RIV(ET)ER. The Tyne and the Clyde were both great British shipbuilding rivers, which is why the surface feels so natural.
explanation.definitionFit: Riveters fastened steel plates on hulls, a classic job in shipyards.

clue.text: Retreats, potentially, with mass movement out of control

parts.note: spas are places to retreat to, given as an example
M is the symbol for mass in physics

explanation.surface: People fleeing in a crowd that has got out of hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retreats' looks like a verb about withdrawing, but it is a plural noun for restful places.
explanation.definitionFit: A spasm is an involuntary muscle contraction, a movement the body cannot control.

clue.text: South America greeting Japanese dish

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for south
the US is America
hi is a casual hello

explanation.surface: A continent welcoming a dish from Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South America' reads as one continent, but it splits into the south abbreviation and the US.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is the Japanese dish of vinegared rice with raw fish or other toppings.

clue.text: Contents of course as opposed to previous one

parts.note: anti means against
past means former or previous
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Course material compared with an earlier course, like a syllabus review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' suggests a programme of study; it is a course of a meal, the starter.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasti are the Italian appetisers served as a first course of a meal.

clue.text: Current fashion trend ignoring the odds

parts.note: a mode is a fashion or style

indicators.note: skipping the odd-numbered positions leaves only the even letters of the word

parts.note: second and fourth letters of the word

explanation.surface: Following the latest fashion while betting against the bookies' odds.
explanation.definitionFit: Modern means belonging to the present time, which is what current means.

clue.text: Religious assembly — following conclusions of that, sign agreement

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the agreement word is placed after the selected letters
conclusions are endings, and 'that' points back to the words just read, so take their final letters

parts.note: final letter of the first word
final letter of the second word
a nod signals that you agree

explanation.surface: A church council signs an accord after concluding its business.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition does double duty: 'that' refers back to 'Religious assembly', whose two last letters start the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A synod is a formal council of church clergy and officials.

clue.text: Called again for version of bible without it

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the bible version sits around the last word

parts.note: the Revised Version is a nineteenth-century English Bible translation
taken as written

explanation.surface: A caller returns for a different Bible translation that leaves something out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like it means lacking, but here it is the older sense of outside: REVIS(IT)ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To revisit is to call on a place or person again, so called again is its past tense.

clue.text: Male is found acting inappropriately

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for male
taken as written
to found metal is to cast it in a mould

explanation.surface: A man is caught behaving badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' looks like the past of find; it is the verb for making metal objects in a foundry.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor miscast is playing an unsuitable role, performing in a part that does not fit them.

clue.text: Holiday-maker who's having bad experience in fall?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a day ..., someone on an outing

definitions.text: who's having bad experience in fall?
definitions.meaning: second meaning, punning: one on a bad drug trip, or one who stumbles over

explanation.walkthrough: The second half packs two puns: a bad trip is a bad drug experience, and tripping is how a fall starts. 'Fall' also hints at an autumn holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A tripper is a tourist on a short excursion, and also slang for someone under hallucinogens.

clue.text: The aspirator I'd ordered as medical specialist

indicators.note: ordered means put into a fresh sequence, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone says they ordered a suction device for a hospital doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A radiotherapist is a medical practitioner who treats disease, especially cancer, with radiation.

clue.text: Food expert set up feast with artist

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means raised so it reads from the bottom upward

parts.note: Eid is a Muslim festival, a feast
Titian was the Venetian Renaissance painter

explanation.surface: A nutrition expert lays on a banquet alongside a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: Eid is the festival ending Ramadan, celebrated with feasting; 'set up' works because this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A dietitian is a trained specialist in nutrition and diets.

clue.text: Stupidly intransigent, like an inhuman revolution

definitions.meaning: second meaning, punning: a revolt led by animals, as in Animal Farm, has pigs at its head

explanation.walkthrough: In Orwell's Animal Farm the pigs lead the animals' revolt, so a revolution that isn't human might well be headed by pigs.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigheaded means obstinately stubborn, refusing to change one's mind however foolish.

clue.text: One appearing in awful cabaret, cause of complaints

indicators.note: appearing in puts one piece inside the jumbled word
something awful is in a terrible state, so these letters are muddled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A performer in a dreadful nightclub show draws complaints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaints' looks like grumbles from an audience; it means illnesses.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacteria are microbes that cause many infections, and complaints here means ailments.

clue.text: Orientating car hopelessly in unfamiliar area

indicators.note: done hopelessly means done in a muddle, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A driver struggling to point the car the right way in strange territory.
explanation.definitionFit: Terra incognita is Latin for unknown land, used of any territory or subject not yet explored.

clue.text: Temporary fit around either end for example

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the fitness phrase wraps the single letter

parts.note: in trim means fit and in good condition

indicators.note: either end means one of its two terminal letters, which here are identical

parts.note: the word begins and ends with the same letter

explanation.surface: A temporary fitting placed around the ends of something as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: IN T(E)RIM: 'either end' works because both ends of the word example are the same letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Interim describes an arrangement lasting only until something permanent replaces it, just as temporary does.

clue.text: Part of church with window on left

parts.note: a window of opportunity is a chance
L for left, placed on after the first piece

explanation.surface: A church area with a stained-glass window on its left side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Window' suggests church glass but means an opportunity.
explanation.definitionFit: The chancel is the area of a church near the altar, used by clergy and choir.

clue.text: China as location of storm that's blown up

definitions.text: China as location of storm that's blown up

parts.note: surface reading: the country where a weather system struck
setter's reading: a piece of crockery, where a fuss blown out of proportion proverbially happens

explanation.walkthrough: China is crockery, and 'a storm in a' small cup of it is the idiom for a fuss that has been blown up out of all proportion.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom storm in a teacup names a trivial row, so the cup is the storm's location and is a piece of china.

clue.text: Leave without information that's urgently necessary

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so the departing word surrounds the information word

parts.note: to exit is to leave
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Departing without being told anything that's urgently needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' seems to mean lacking, but it means outside: EXI(GEN)T.
explanation.definitionFit: Exigent means pressing or demanding immediate action, so it describes what is urgently needed.

clue.text: With fine heading, this communication might sound womanly

indicators.note: the heading is extra: once its first letter is taken away again, what remains is the answer
might sound means is said like, so the word is judged by its pronunciation

parts.note: the word for womanly, spelt as F plus the message word
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil grades; it is the part removed

explanation.surface: A nicely titled message that comes across as feminine.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: put F (fine) at the head of the answer and the result is pronounced like the word for womanly.
explanation.definitionFit: An email is an electronic message, a form of communication.

clue.text: No backing in a wager that's on hold

indicators.note: in places the reversed word inside the gamble phrase

parts.note: a, plus bet for wager

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the refusal word is read in reverse

parts.note: nay is an old word for no

explanation.surface: A bet left unsettled because nobody would back it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' sounds like supporting a bet, but it signals reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Abeyant means in abeyance, suspended or temporarily set aside, which is being on hold.

clue.text: Something bent accountant set up producing capital

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means raised so the pieces read from the bottom upward

parts.note: an arc is a curved line
CA is chartered accountant

explanation.surface: A crooked accountant is framed and makes off with capital money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money; it is a capital city. Bent also invites the slang sense of crooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Accra is the capital city of Ghana.

clue.text: It's gallant and smart embracing demolished rival

indicators.note: embracing means hugging round, so the stylish word wraps the other

parts.note: chic means smart and stylish

indicators.note: something demolished is knocked down and its parts lie jumbled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dashing suitor, well dressed, hugs the rival he has just beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Chivalric relates to the knightly code of chivalry, so it describes courteous, gallant behaviour.

clue.text: Domestic arrangement as Johnson, say, houses author

indicators.note: houses means gives shelter to, so one word is held inside the other

parts.note: Dr Johnson, the eighteenth-century lexicographer, is the classic example of a doctor
Umberto Eco, Italian author of The Name of the Rose

explanation.surface: A politician named Johnson putting a writer up at home.
explanation.walkthrough: Johnson invites thoughts of a prime minister, but it is Dr Johnson, giving the doctor abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Decor is the furnishing and decoration of a room, how a home is arranged.

clue.text: Write a line about Crime and Punishment

definitions.note: adjective phrase: relating to punishment for crime

parts.note: to pen is to write
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Instructions to jot down a comment on Dostoevsky's novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The novel title is the definition: the answer is the adjective concerning crimes and their punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Penal means relating to the punishment of offenders, as in penal code or penal colony.

clue.text: Daughter in bad role eclipsed by mother in sensational performance

indicators.note: in puts the daughter abbreviation inside the jumbled letters
being eclipsed means covered over, so the parent word surrounds the rest

parts.note: mama is mother

indicators.note: bad means faulty, so the acting-part word is jumbled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A daughter cast in a poor part is upstaged by her mother in an over-the-top show.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: the daughter goes inside the jumbled role, and that whole group sits inside the mother word.
explanation.definitionFit: A melodrama is a play with exaggerated, sensational plot and emotion.
